title: The error term in the truncated Perron formula for the logarithm of an L-function: the sharp eight-prime sieve bound (Lemma 6)
author: Stephan Ramon Garcia, Jeffrey Lagarias, Ethan Simpson Lee
work: The error term in the truncated Perron formula for the logarithm of an L-function
difficulty_reason: Counted unit: the article's sharp eight-prime sieve bound, printed as Lemma 6 (source0.tex lines 295--314, source label Lemma:Sieve30), which bounds the reciprocal-distance sums F_1(x) over the largest eight primes below x and F_2(x) over the smallest eight primes above x by the explicit rational constant C = 1284699552/444215525 = 2.89206..., and which the article asserts to be sharp in both directions. It is delivered with the article's own proof at source0.tex lines 336--369 (34 lines), the proof block whose parts (a) and (b) prove exactly those two bounds; the block sits after the figure that illustrates it, and the structure analysis did not link it to the statement, but the correspondence is literal: (a) evaluates the case x <= 9.5 and then the extremal residue pattern modulo 30 of the eight primes in (x/2,x), and (b) does the same for (x,3x/2), each ending with the same constant C. The author proof is complete as printed: the only quoted background is the classical residue classification of primes greater than 5 modulo 30, and the finite verifications the authors state they performed are part of the printed proof and are retained verbatim rather than hidden. H3: an original sharp explicit estimate with a complete, self-contained case-analysis proof; it is short and elementary in its ingredients, but it is the authors' own calibrated computation rather than a restatement of a textbook bound or a formal consequence of a cited theorem.
